Medical History

- Current health concerns and risk factors:
  • 3-day history of profuse watery diarrhea (≈hourly while awake), crampy central lower-abdominal pain (intermittent, self-rated ~6/10), associated nausea and occasional vomiting (worse after milk), subjective fever, reduced urine frequency.  
  • Possible infective gastroenteritis (brother experienced similar illness 5 days prior).  
  • Risk of dehydration.

- Relevant family medical history:
  • Father: stage III colon (bowel) cancer.  
  • Brother: acute diarrheal illness (current, improving).  
  • Other family history not recorded.

- Medications (including OTC or shared medications):
  • Paracetamol (acetaminophen) – OTC, dose/route/frequency not documented.  
  • Advised to purchase oral rehydration solution (e.g., Dioralyte); not yet commenced.  
  • No regular prescribed medications.

- Immunisation status reviewed: Not recorded.

- Sexual and reproductive health: Not recorded.

- Physical activity and nutrition:
  • Nutrition: Frequently buys takeaway; currently tolerating only liquids/soft foods → diarrhea soon after eating.  
  • Physical activity level not recorded.

- Alcohol, tobacco, and substance use:
  • Cigarettes: Social smoker, “on a Friday,” not daily; quantity not specified.  
  • Alcohol: Occasional beer on weekdays; binge drinking once or twice per month (“drink a lot” with friends).  
  • Other substances: Not recorded.

- Hearing loss or concerns: Not recorded.

- Mood/mental health (including depression, self-harm risk): Not specifically assessed; reports difficulty managing work while unwell but no mood symptoms disclosed.

- Vision problems or recent changes: Not recorded (patient could not see clinician on video due to connection issue; not a vision complaint).

- Family and social relationships, caring responsibilities:
  • Lives with mother and sister; brother lives elsewhere.  
  • Works in a government office (central London).  
  • No caring responsibilities noted.

Management Plan

- Working diagnosis: Acute infective gastroenteritis with risk of dehydration.
- Advice provided:
  • Maintain hydration: clear fluids plus pharmacy-purchased oral rehydration solution (e.g., Dioralyte).  
  • Soft diet (soups, mashed foods) and gradual re-introduction of solids as tolerated.  
  • Continue paracetamol for fever or abdominal discomfort (dose per package instructions).  
  • Avoid alcohol while symptomatic.
- Safety-netting / follow-up:
  • If diarrhea, vomiting, or fever persist beyond 48 hours, or signs of dehydration develop, patient to call back for reassessment and possible further investigations.  
  • Educated on warning signs (ongoing high fever, inability to keep fluids down, reduced urine output).
- No prescriptions issued.  
- No referrals at this stage.

Consider (discuss at future visit):
  • CTG registration and preventive health check reminders.  
  • Smoking cessation support and alcohol harm-minimization.  
  • Bowel cancer screening plan given family history.  
  • Routine immunization review and preventive screening (e.g., mental health, STI if sexually active).
